newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sells 80 billion bolivars TEM bills.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sells 80 billion bolivars TEM bills.

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank said it sold 50 billion bolivars of 179-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills at a price of 100.21 percent.
The 179-day bills carried a 29.34 percent coupon.

The bank also sold 15 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 30.39 percent coupon at a price of 98.34 percent, and 15 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 31.48 percent coupon at an average price of 97.99 percent.

According to a preliminary calculation by Reuters using the Central Bank's method, the yield on the notes was 28.86 percent for the 179-day TEMs, 33.16 percent on the 269-day notes, and 34.19 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
At last week's auction, the bank sold 173-, 262- and 351-day bills with yields of 29.27, 33.64 and 35.50 percent respectively.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
